content:
anya: Heads-up: customer reported a provisional token blip during a stream where client truncated mid-toolcall. trace=invtrunc-9

sam: Ack. Is this the same pattern as previous truncation/rerun dupes?

anya: Similar but twist: client sent the same invocation_id on retry, ledger still minted another provisional.

leo: Do we have logs?

anya: ```
[2025-06-14T14:02:01Z] stream.recv session=s-77 partial=true truncated_by_client=true invocation_id=inv-9
[2025-06-14T14:02:01Z] toolcall.start invocation_id=inv-9 provisional=pv-77
[2025-06-14T14:02:02Z] retry-scheduler queued invocation_id=inv-9
[2025-06-14T14:02:03Z] toolcall.start invocation_id=inv-9 provisional=pv-78
[2025-06-14T14:02:04Z] toolcall.confirm invocation_id=inv-9 confirmed=420
```

zack: So two provisionals (pv-77 & pv-78) for same invocation_id. Ledger dedupe key is provisional id only.

sam: Short-term mitigation: suppress automatic retry on client-truncated events for a short window, or have retry reuse provisional if invocation_id present.

leo: Long-term: ledger idempotency on (invocation_id, session) when invocation_id exists. Also add `charge_reason` and `invocation_id` to billing telemetry so console can group.

ops-bot: Runbook entry runbook/toolcall/truncate-dedupe created. Owner: leo. ETA 48h.

anya: UX: console should show provisional vs confirmed columns and a "stale provisional" button to mark/refund quickly.

sam: Plan: implement ledger shadow dedupe (emit header x-dedupe-decision), add probe metric `invocation_provisional_dup_count`, add console column and refund CTA. Canary 1% for 4h.

zack: I'll add alerts if dup rate >0.1% for any customer region.

anya: Thanks — I'll tell support to hold refunds until shadow run completes. :thumbsup:
